content.headline: Eighteen Teams, One Hundred Eighty Picks, and Somebody Really Did Take Cade With Cade and Friends
content.intro:
The board opened exactly the way the fellowship hall predicted it would: the two biggest humans in the league went first and second, Jokić at the top and Wembanyama right behind him, and then the guards came in a wave. Luka, Shai, Cade, Maxey, Ant, Haliburton, LaMelo, Mitchell, Brunson — nine of the first eighteen picks were backcourt, which is either a philosophy or a very polite stampede.

The slide of the night belonged to Cooper Flagg, who sat there until the fifteenth pick while people chased proven names. The turn at the end of round one was the sweetest seat in the room: Brunson at eighteen and Curry at nineteen, back to back, no waiting.

After that it got interesting. Joel Embiid didn't come off the board until the fifty-fifth pick. Damian Lillard waited until the fifty-ninth, Ja Morant until the eighty-fifth, and Zion until the ninety-second — a whole tier of household names going in the rounds where people usually draft handcuffs. Meanwhile the rookies went early and often: Dybantsa at fifty-four, Cameron Boozer at sixty-four, Caleb Wilson at eighty-three, Darryn Peterson at one hundred eighteen.

And from round seven on, it was centers, centers, centers. Hartenstein, Claxton, Poeltl, Turner, Mitchell Robinson, Gafford, Missi — if you waited on size, you waited about four picks too long.
content.outro:
So there it is: one hundred eighty picks, several very tall rosters, one roster that may never grab a rebound, and eighteen people absolutely certain they got the steal of the draft. Everybody is undefeated this morning, which is the best any of us will feel until the first injury report lands.

Set your lineups, check who's playing four games in week one, and be kind in the group chat. We'll find out soon enough whose plan survives contact with an actual Tuesday night.

See you Sunday — and at the first tip.jj Good luck, all.

(Correction: that typo is staying. It's tradition now.)

team_notes.prose: First in the preseason order, and the draft reads like it: Brunson and Curry scooped up back to back at eighteen and nineteen, then Dybantsa and Embiid grabbed in the same breath at fifty-four and fifty-five. Gordon, Brooks, Porziņģis and Caruso round it out, so the depth is real — the whole thing just needs the Embiid swing to land the way they're hoping.

Shai at four and then a frontcourt built on long arms, with Mobley at thirty-three and Jaren Jackson Jr. at forty — if the rim protection holds up, that's a very uncomfortable team to shoot against. Knueppel, Pritchard, Braun and DeRozan give them floor spacing, though a lot rides on Shai being the engine every single week.

Letting Flagg fall to fifteen was the league's gift and they took it, then added Barnes and Kyrie for a versatile, position-flexible core. Okongwu, Randle and Wendell Carter Jr. keep the frontcourt honest, and taking two more rookies in Ace Bailey and Mikel Brown Jr. at the end is a cheerful little bet on the future.

The team name is WEE-TOO-TALL and the draft board agrees: LeBron, Anthony Davis and Siakam up top, then Sharpe, Claxton, Gafford and Diabaté stacked in the back half. That is a lot of size on one roster, and the guard chairs — Herro, Dylan Harper, Jeremiah Fears — will have to carry more than their share.

Luka at three and Bam at thirty-four is about as sturdy a spine as you can build, and Brandon Miller at thirty-nine gives it some upside. The back half is all useful glue — Hart, McCollum, Sheppard, Herb Jones — which is the kind of roster that doesn't wow you in June and quietly wins you weeks in January.

They had the very first pick, took Jokić, and then doubled down on size with Duren at thirty-six before swinging back for Harden at thirty-seven. Naz Reid, Queta and P.J. Washington mean the rebounding should be absurd; the guard room after Harden and Suggs is where the season gets decided.

Giannis at seven and Booker at thirty is a tidy one-two, and then they went shot-blocking shopping with Kessler at forty-three and Alex Sarr at sixty-six. Nembhard, VanVleet and Anthony Black are steady hands at guard, though three young bigs on one roster means some patience is built into the plan.

Towns at sixteen and Trae at twenty-one off the turn is a fun pairing — one of the best shooting bigs in the league next to a maestro. Then Zubac at fifty-seven and Poeltl at one twenty-four joined the party, which is a lot of center for one roster, and Edgecombe, Barrett and Mathurin give the wings some pop.

Anthony Edwards and Chet in the first two rounds, then Gobert at eighty-two, which means the paint is basically closed for business. Derrick White, Jrue Holiday and Darryn Peterson give the backcourt a nice mix of now and later, and Keegan Murray and Vassell are the shooting that has to show up.

Tatum, Jamal Murray, Jalen Williams and then Cameron Boozer at sixty-four — that's a wing collection with a genuine rookie lottery ticket attached. Paul George and Ingram add scoring punch if the health cooperates, but outside of Isaiah Jackson at one seventy-two there isn't a lot of true center on this board.

Wembanyama at two and then Markkanen and Sabonis back to back at thirty-five and thirty-eight: an unapologetically enormous frontcourt. Fox and Rollins handle the backcourt, and Hartenstein, Kuminga and Jerami Grant later means they'll have more quality bigs than lineup slots most weeks — a good problem, but a problem.

Jalen Johnson and Amen Thompson in the first two rounds is a bet on length and chaos, and Paolo at forty-eight makes that frontcourt genuinely scary on paper. They then took Jarrett Allen, Maluach, Nurkić and Raynaud, so the center spot is fortified several times over, with Garland the one that really has to hit at guard.

Donovan Mitchell at seventeen and Kevin Durant at twenty is a lovely way to use a turn, and Clingan at fifty-three is the kind of pick that makes sense before anyone else is ready to make it. Zion at ninety-two is the upside swing of the night, and taking two different Georges — Keyonte and Kyshawn — is a bold commitment to confusing the commissioner.

Maxey at eight, then Trey Murphy, Bane and Michael Porter Jr. — this is a roster made almost entirely of wings who shoot, and if the threes fall it'll be a fun scoreboard. The catch is that the closest thing to a true center is Collin Murray-Boyles and Draymond, so the rebounding plan will need some creativity.

Truth in advertising: Cade and friends took Cade at five, and then went and got the friends — Giddey, Kawhi, Dejounte Murray. Ware, Collins, Missi and Vučević give them plenty of frontcourt bodies, and if Kawhi at forty-one plays a full load, that's the pick everyone points to later.

LaMelo, Jaylen Brown, LaVine and Ja is a backcourt that will absolutely put up numbers and will also require a healthy prayer list. Jaden McDaniels and Peyton Watson supply the defense, but outside of them this roster is guards and wings all the way down — they'll need the boards from somewhere.

Haliburton at eleven is a bet with real conviction behind it, and Avdija and Franz Wagner at twenty-six and forty-seven give the wings a solid floor. Stephon Castle and Jared McCain are nice young swings, and Caleb Wilson at eighty-three was earlier than most rooms would have gone — which is exactly how you look smart in March.

Şengün at fourteen and Reaves at twenty-three is a genuinely fun foundation, and Dyson Daniels at fifty is the kind of pick that quietly wins categories. After that it's guard after guard — Lillard, Davion Mitchell, Quickley, Kevin Porter Jr. — so Şengün, Butler and Jalen Smith are carrying the frontcourt load by themselves.
